subject.title: [Bug]: codex agent fails ("exited with code 1") — macOS XProtect deletes bundled @openai/codex@0.128.0 as malware; codex-acp@0.0.44 pins the flagged version

question: Should acpx fix this Codex/XProtect failure by bumping the built-in `codex-acp` range, by adding a system-`codex` `CODEX_PATH` fallback, or by documenting only the workaround?
rationale: The adapter range and fallback behavior are user-visible built-in agent conventions, and the issue already carries product-decision/no-new-fix-pr labels; automation should not choose the permanent Codex launch policy on its own.

options.title: Bump and document first
options.body: Update the built-in `codex-acp` range after ACP compatibility smokes and document `CODEX_PATH` as the supported workaround for affected macOS hosts.

options.title: Add fallback too
options.body: Also inject `CODEX_PATH` from a resolved system `codex` when unset, accepting the added built-in agent convention and testing explicit-env precedence.

options.title: Document only
options.body: Leave the built-in range unchanged and document manual config or `CODEX_PATH`, accepting that fresh affected users may still hit the broken default.

recommendation.title: Bump and document first
recommendation.body: Update the built-in `codex-acp` range after ACP compatibility smokes and document `CODEX_PATH` as the supported workaround for affected macOS hosts.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the most recent release/range history on the built-in adapter surface, while the final choice affects release defaults and docs.
